Base Mercedes-AMG GT SUV Receives CGI Pure Stock Treatment: Black Plastics, Steelies, Manual Windows
8 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV , which has a dedicated EV architecture and no correspondent in the Mercedes-Benz family, is the 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe’s high riding sibling, and they show major similarities while being rather unique propositions on the automotive market – arriving sometime in 2027.
The automotive world is going to extremes as of late: some carmakers are going back to the roots of affordability with base models like the Citroen 2CV concept seen recently at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, while others only seem to think that the most powerful and exclusive vehicles matter nowadays.
The roster of such models includes things like the Mercedes- AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, or the Ferrari Luce and the newly introduced Jaguar Type 01, recently. Actually, Mercedes is doubling the gamble with the newly introduced GT SUV, too, which is a high-performance model for the high-end. Kind of like the new Bentley Torcal, but with a focus on sportiness rather than outright opulence. Well, if you’re not into six-figure automobiles and would rather see the carmakers go back to making affordable, attainable models, no worries – there’s a solution.
Albeit it comes from the parallel universes of vehicular CGI thanks to a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators. More precisely, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the new 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV and included it in his new series of CGI ‘Pure Stock’ models.
The latter also includes the Jaguar Type 01, the all-new G50 BMW 3 Series, the Bentley Torcal all-electric crossover ultra-SUV, the latest Audi Q7, or the G65 BMW X5 and iX5, among others. The pixel master probably started the series as an experiment, but since it has become quite successful, he continues to morph the latest novelties from controversial experiments into ‘mundane’ models that anyone could probably afford due to the cost-cutting measures.
More precisely, the new Mercedes-AMG GT SUV gets dressed in a base , non-metallic white hue, adopts a simpler front fascia with black plastic radiator grilles and a basic bumper, has black plastic protection elements all around the lower parts of the body, and also mixes steel wheels with simple roof rails and a cheap rear diffuser.
The author does keep the hidden door handles and paints the exterior mirrors, as this is a premium model, after all (sic). Moving inside, the situation is even more hilarious: the triple-screen setup has disappeared in favor of separate small-sized displays for the instrument cluster and the infotainment system, for example.
Additionally, the three dials on the central tunnel are now up on the dashboard as manual controls for the AC, and all the upholstery elements are plain and simple gray cloth. There are still some premium touches like the steering wheel and the carbon fiber on the door handles or the center tunnel, but even the front windows now have hand cranks!
